name: Skincareholic routines

card.summary: Long, many-step skincare routines shown by creators, aimed at clearer, smoother, more even skin through layers of cleansers, toners, serums and moisturisers.
card.note: Over-exfoliating or over-washing can irritate skin and damage the skin barrier.

quick.overview:
"Skincareholic" routines are lengthy, multi-step skin regimens that creators film and share. The goal is visible skin improvement: clearer, more even, hydrated skin.

Basic skin care has a few steps: cleansing, moisturising and sun protection, with exfoliation as an option. Longer routines add products such as toners, serums, essences and ampoules.
quick.how: Creators layer cleanser, toner, serum or essence, moisturiser and sunscreen, sometimes with exfoliating acids and masks on set days. Routines are shared as videos and product lists.
quick.risks: Dermatology sources caution that excessive exfoliation can irritate skin and damage the barrier, and overwashing may cause dryness. Leave-on products such as serums and essences can contain fragrances and preservatives that cause allergies in some people.

lead: Skincareholic routines are long, multi-step skincare routines presented by creators and enthusiasts. They are used to pursue clearer, smoother and more even skin.

Standard skin care includes cleansing, exfoliation, moisturising and sun protection; the longer routines add layers of toners, serums, ampoules and boosters, which are leave-on products that may contain fragrance and preservatives.[1]
Reference sources note that excessive exfoliation can cause irritation and barrier damage, and that overwashing can dry skin.[1]

chain: Cleanse, treat, moisturise and protect in layers
angle.text: Multi-step routines are used to improve skin texture, hydration and tone, each step targeting one concern.
